name: @skarn-security/skarn

tools.name: scan_sessions
tools.description: Scan this machine's AI coding assistant session transcripts for leaked credentials and risky agent behaviour, and return the redacted JSON report as a text block. Each detected secret is reported in a truncated mask that keeps at most its first character and last two characters; the surrounding transcript snippet and the transcript-authored project label are not returned. severity sets the lowest reported level, hours bounds the window (0 scans all history and is the slowest form), project narrows to one project, user narrows to the user ids or email addresses a Compliance API export recorded. compliance_withheld counts the Compliance API export sessions that were found and withheld unread because reading them needs an Enterprise license; they contribute nothing to the counts.

severity.description: Lowest severity to report. Default low.

hours.description: Only sessions active in the last N hours. 0 scans all history. Default 0.

project.description: Only sessions whose project name or path matches this filter.

user.description: Only sessions whose user id or email address matches this filter; only a Compliance API export carries either.

tools.name: vet_configs
tools.description: Statically vet this machine's AI assistant configuration - hook commands, MCP server definitions, permission grants, installed plugins and skills - and return the masked JSON findings report as a text block. Read-only: config files are opened for reading and never written. Project-level configuration is read from this server process's working directory.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List recent AI coding assistant sessions as structural metadata only: session id, assistant, timestamps, message and tool counts, and token totals. No session message text is returned, and no label authored inside a transcript such as a project name, git branch or model id. hours bounds the window, limit caps the row count, project, cli and user narrow the list; a row from a Compliance API export carries the recorded user id and never the email address. compliance_withheld counts the Compliance API export sessions that were found and withheld unread because reading them needs an Enterprise license; they contribute no row.

hours.description: Only sessions active in the last N hours. 0 lists all history. Default 168.

project.description: Only sessions whose project name or path matches this filter.

user.description: Only sessions whose user id or email address matches this filter; only a Compliance API export carries either.

cli.description: Only sessions recorded by this assistant, for example claude, codex or cursor.

tools.name: session_stats
tools.description: Aggregate recent AI coding assistant sessions into counts: sessions per assistant, total messages, distinct projects, token totals and estimated cost. No session message text is returned. hours bounds the window, project, cli and user narrow what is aggregated. compliance_withheld counts the Compliance API export sessions that were found and withheld unread because reading them needs an Enterprise license; they contribute nothing to the counts.

hours.description: Only sessions active in the last N hours. 0 aggregates all history. Default 168.

project.description: Only sessions whose project name or path matches this filter.

user.description: Only sessions whose user id or email address matches this filter; only a Compliance API export carries either.

cli.description: Only sessions recorded by this assistant, for example claude, codex or cursor.

instructions: Skarn exposes read-only tools over this machine's own AI coding assistant sessions and configuration. Every tool runs locally and makes no network call. Scan results are redacted: every value a detector matched is returned only in a truncated mask that keeps at most its first character and last two characters and discards the middle. These tools return findings, configuration issues and session metadata, never session message text and never a label authored inside a transcript such as a project name, a git branch, a model id or a tool name. Three strings are passed through as they are, because they are the locators you act on: a file path, a session id and a timestamp. The user id and workspace id a Compliance API export recorded are passed through the same way, and the email address it recorded never appears. No tool writes, changes or removes a file.
